I lead the global record to report meeting every year, and I want to tell you about the best comment I ever heard there. It did not come from a manager. It came from an analyst in Poland, in her second year with the company. Everybody was quiet after my presentation, and she said: sorry to jump in, but can I build on one point? Then she described a small change in how her team did reconciliations, and it saved us two days in the close. Later she told me she was terrified, and that her English was not perfect. Honestly, I did not notice. What I noticed was that she spoke up when nobody else did. So if you have an idea in my meeting, do not wait until your English is ready. Raise your hand. The idea is what we remember.

I train finance teams before international conferences, and the first thing I tell them is this: small talk is not about being interesting. It is about being interested. You do not need a brilliant icebreaker. A simple question works, like how was your flight, or which entity are you from? Then listen, and ask one more question about the answer. Most of my clients are afraid of the silence after the first question, so they talk about themselves for five minutes. Please do not do that. And here is a small trick: question tags. You say, it is a big event, isn't it? and the other person almost always agrees and keeps talking. When the coffee break ends, you have not given a speech. You have made a contact. Try to mingle with three new people before lunch. That is enough.
